title: SDK Launchpad: sample collection for low-latency streaming, retries, and CLI ergonomics
creator: Samantha Ortiz
description: Create a compact, opinionated collection of language-specific sample apps and cookbook snippets that demonstrate production-fit patterns for low-latency streaming, robust retry policies, and ergonomic CLI/HTTP server integrations across Next.js (TS), FastAPI (Python), and Go. The goal is an easily consumable Launchpad repository that engineers can clone, run locally, and adapt to their apps while illustrating trade-offs (latency vs batching), graceful fallbacks, and cost-conscious behaviors.
acceptance_criteria: A single repo `sdks/launchpad` contains 4 runnable examples: Next.js streaming chat, FastAPI streaming proxy, Go minimal inference server, and a cross-platform CLI example.
Each example includes a README with start instructions, environment variables, and a short section on production hardening (timeouts, metrics, graceful shutdown).
Streaming examples exhibit sub-second first-token latency for short prompts in local dev and include a documented browser-side incremental renderer for Next.js.
Retry semantics implemented in each example: idempotency keys where applicable, exponential backoff with jitter, and a circuit-breaker note for high failure rates.
At least two automated smoke tests validate the end-to-end examples in CI (one for streaming correctness, one for retry behavior).
Developer docs (confluence) and a GitHub repo with at least one merged PR and two reviewers' approvals.
deliverables: User-facing READMEs and quickstart scripts (makefile or npm script) per example
One documented retry policy module in each language and a cross-language README explaining parity
CI workflow that runs smoke tests on PRs and nightly sample validation
Short how-to blog + example screenshots for the docs site
out_of_scope: Production-grade deployment manifests for every cloud provider (we will include a single example for k8s but not per-cloud templates)
Full SDK refactors or API surface changes — these are users of the existing SDKs, not API redesigns
test_plan: CI smoke test: start example server, send short streaming request, assert first-token arrives within 900ms
Retry test: run flaky mock endpoint that fails 2/3 times; client should succeed within 3 retries and log backoff intervals
Linting and unit tests for the retry modules in each language
Manual local UX run-through documenting developer setup on macOS and Linux
rollout_plan: Merge to main when two reviewers approve and CI smoke tests pass
Ship initial docs page under /docs/sdk-launchpad and link from SDK quickstart
Announce in #dev and schedule a 30-minute demo for Solutions and Docs teams
Collect feedback for two weeks and iterate on the most confusing patterns
comments: 2026-02-11 - Samantha Ortiz: Kickoff meeting notes added to Confluence. Agreed on four canonical examples to keep scope tight. Decided to prefer SSE/chunked HTTP for browser streaming; WebSocket optional.

2026-02-18 - Ravi Patel: PoC Next.js streaming renderer completed. First-token rendering achieved at ~450ms on local dev with a tiny prompt. Found edge case: Node 18 vs 20 behavior requires conditional API (experimental fetch streaming).

2026-02-22 - Design review (Ilya Chen): UX suggestion to expose a single "onPartial" callback in the TypeScript sample rather than raw stream handling to make incremental hydration approachable for app devs.

2026-02-27 - Engineering note: Chose exponential backoff with full jitter (base=200ms, cap=5s, maxAttempts=5) as default. Will include a small code comment on when to lower attempts for latency-sensitive flows.
2026-03-01 - PR feedback (reviewer: Priya Shah): Request to add a metrics counter example for 'retry_count' and a sample Prometheus job scraped from the Go server. Added to deliverables.
2026-03-03 - QA: Discovered flaky streaming test in CI related to container CPU throttling. Implemented a CI shim that increases CPU quota for smoke test jobs. CI now stable on retry test.
2026-03-05 - Ravi Patel: Merged FastAPI streaming proxy PR. Next up: finalize README and add the cross-language parity doc.
notes: Trade-offs: We prioritize reproducible dev-onboarding and clarity over exhaustive coverage. The samples will point to runtime tuning docs for production performance optimizations.
Consider adding a small 'lite' deployment manifest for k8s to show readiness/liveness and resource requests, but keep it optional in the initial launch.
Plan to extract the retry module into the main SDK if adoption is high; initial placement is inside the launchpad repo for quick iteration.
